- Foreign students who earn an associate degree or higher in Taiwan can apply to extend their stay for up to two years. [1]
- During the extended stay, graduates are not subject to restrictions on the types of professional or technical jobs they can take, employer qualifications or minimum salary thresholds. [1]
- They can work in any field as long as they comply with labor laws, and after the extended stay ends, can transition to other residency programs based on a points system or regulations governing foreign professionals. [1]

- A bachelor's degree takes four years and at least 128 credits in total. [3]
- The university adopts the system of academic years and course credits. [3]

- 12 extra graduation credits must be earned for admission on an equivalent qualification, excluding military training and PE. [4]
- Military training and PE do not count toward the 12 extra credits. [4]

- At least 16 credits each semester in years one to three and at least 9 credits each semester in year four. [5]
- Taking fewer credits requires approval from your advisor and department head; without it you can be dismissed. [5]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [5]

- International students take the full-year five-credit course “Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students” instead of the 3-credit Chinese (A) and 2-credit Chinese (B) courses. [1]
- This is specified in Article 3 of the common-course regulations, which states that overseas Chinese and international students must take the five-credit course. [1]
- The requirement is detailed in the NCU Regulations on Common Course Selection and Requirements, Article 3. [1]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- 6 credits of Mandarin courses at the Language Center [2]
- File for the Chinese course substitution before you graduate [2]
- This differs from Article 3 of the common-course regulations (5 credits of Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students) [2]

- PE is required for five semesters: Freshman PE I and II plus three PE interest electives. [3]
- PE carries no graduation credits. [3]
- After the five semesters you may take a 1-credit PE course, which also does not count toward graduation. [3]

- The minimum credit requirement for a master's degree is 24 credits, not counting thesis credits. [4]
- Each department sets its own graduation rules, but the minimum is 24 credits. [4]
- You must also take at least one graduate course of 1 credit or more at NCU; waived courses do not count. [4]
- The requirement is stated in National Central University Study Regulations, Article 58. [4]

- At least 34 credits are required for direct admission into a doctoral program, including at least 18 doctoral-level credits, not counting dissertation credits. [5]
- The remaining credits must be taken from the doctoral program. [5]

- Apply before the add/drop deadline of your first semester [1]
- If approved, you skip both semesters and receive 6 credits that count toward graduation [1]
- Contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 for application [1]
- The application process is case‑by‑case review [1]

- Undergraduates need at least 100 service hours on the NCU passport before they can receive the degree certificate. [2]
- You can check the hours on the Service Learning Website or in the Graduation System. [2]
- If you have any questions, contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs at https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/. [2]

- Service learning is not listed among the graduation conditions for master's and doctoral students. [4]
- The graduation conditions for master's and doctoral students are courses and credits, the degree examination, and conduct grades. [4]
- Individual departments may still set their own requirements. [4]
- Contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs at https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/ for more information. [4]

- The service-learning course must be taken in two semesters. [5]
- The two semesters must have different course numbers. [5]
- The course carries zero credits. [5]
- Contact the Center for Service Learning, Office of Student Affairs at https://service-learning.ncu.edu.tw/ for details. [5]
